correctness.rationale: For all positive integers r,s, the proof explicitly fixes +1/-N symmetric valuations and IR/NS definitions, establishes that enemy-containing blocks force negative utility, shows positive Nash product iff r>=s, removes pure core blocks by strict product-improving merging, and maximizes (sum_i (k_i+1) log k_i) by a strict convexity transfer. It enumerates optimal labeled partitions, and proves Nash-stable structure by a strictly profitable core move between any two core-containing blocks, followed by exhaustive deviation inequalities. The exact literal-payoff finite checker checks all set partitions in the stated range, including r<s, boundary r=s, r=1 and s=1; it supports but cannot replace the analytic all-size proof. Critical boundaries and distinct all-Nash-stable from all-optimal quantifiers verified.

value.rationale: The concrete research gap is the relationship of ordinary Nash stability to the new Nash-welfare objective, where the primary paper only proves contractual stability and exhibits a single incompatibility example. The theorem provides a complete natural network-family classification and an infinite, arbitrarily large sharp separation: even when Nash-stable partitions exist, every one has welfare zero while the exact optimum is positive, refuting every finite Nash-stability welfare approximation bound on this class. The exact optimum and optimizer counts expose a structural core/periphery imbalance phase transition rather than a generic small case or arbitrary numerical slice.
